parts.text: We are accepting applications for a 1-year postdoctoral fellowship for the EDIT-STEM Initiative (

), a collaborative funded project to improve Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI) in STEM via educational technological interventions such as games, videos, and other forms of multimedia.

Position: Postdoctoral Fellow

Deadline: Screening of applicants will begin immediately

Location: Carleton University, Ottawa, Canada

Start date: The position is available immediately, to be started as soon as possible (target start date December 1, 2026)

Duration: 1 year (may be extended subject to satisfactory performance, available budget, and project needs)

Research Project Supervisors

Dr. Sonia Chiasson

Professor, School of Computer Science

Dr. Edward Melcer

Associate Professor, School of Computer Science

Salary

The postdoctoral fellow will be offered a salary of $75,000 CAD per annum, with the additional ability to opt into an extended health and dental benefit plan. The postdoc will be considered unionized and will be a member of PSAC Local 77000. Information on this bargaining unit can be found here:

.

Position Duties and Responsibilities

The overall goal of this research project is the design, development, and evaluation of an interactive web-based learning platform focused on engaging behavioral change in EDI. The target audiences for the educational platform are grad students, faculty members, and professionals in STEM fields. This postdoctoral position is focused on the design, development, and evaluation of web-based educational games. Preliminary work on the project is underway. The incumbent will be expected to contribute to and lead aspects of the following activities:

1. Participatory design work with academic/industry partners and a variety of target user populations

2. Design of educational and persuasive technology games for STEM

3. Implementation of deployment-ready web-based games

4. Implementation of web-based framework to facilitate development of a unified suite of games and educational tools

5. User studies evaluating the games with partner organizations

The ideal candidate will be able to take on many of the following core responsibilities:

· Work closely with the interdisciplinary research team to achieve the goals of the EDIT-STEM initiative

· Mentor undergraduate and graduate trainees, including contributing to training activities

· Conduct research activities in HCI relating to EDI and educational technologies

o Coordinate project activities

o Lead design and implementation of game prototypes grounded in HCI, game design, and pedagogical theory

o Lead software development initiatives of deployment-ready games

o Lead software development of a framework to facilitate a unified suite of games and educational tools

o Conduct participatory design research

o Design and conduct research studies including both qualitative and quantitative methods

· Disseminate research findings, including taking a significant role in publishing high-quality research in international conferences and journals

Job Requirements

· A PhD in a discipline such as Computer Science, Human-Computer Interaction, Game Studies, or related field by start of employment

· Experience with relevant HCI methods and with educational game design/development is needed

· Experience with equity, diversity, and inclusivity initiatives preferred

How to Apply Applications should be compiled into a single PDF and sent to

Applications should include:

(1) A cover letter describing how your background and experience qualifies you for this position, including previous work in HCI, educational game design, and EDI

(2) A curriculum vitae (CV)

(3) Please indicate in your application whether you are currently legally eligible to work in Canada

Two letters of reference will be requested from short-listed candidates.

Screening of applications will start immediately and continue until the position is filled.

Accommodations and Accessibility Should you require a copy of this posting in an alternate format, please contact us as soon as possible and we would be happy to get one to you in a timely manner. We believe in the importance of supporting on the-job success for the incumbent and are pleased to discuss and/or provide specific tools, resources or other requirements for day-to-day work requirements, as needed.

About Carleton University:
Carleton University is a dynamic and innovative research and teaching institution with a national and international reputation as a leader in collaborative teaching and learning, research and governance. To learn more about our university and the City of Ottawa, please visit

.

Carleton University is committed to fostering diversity within its community as a source of excellence, cultural enrichment, and social strength. We welcome those who would contribute to the further diversification of our university including, but not limited to: women; visible minorities; First Nations, Inuit and Métis peoples; persons with disabilities; and persons of any sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression. Carleton understands that career paths vary. Legitimate career interruptions will in no way prejudice the assessment process and their impact will be taken into careful consideration.

We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. If contacted for an interview, please inform us should accommodation be required, and arrangements will be made in a timely manner. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply.
